title: AgentSSL: Can MLE Agents Leverage Unlabeled Data?
lead: AgentSSL treats semi-supervised learning as a search over executable programs. The researchers examine two different challenges: whether agents can discover strong methods from scarce labels and abundant unlabeled data, and whether those methods can be selected reliably without trustworthy validation.
question: Can agents find a strong learning strategy when labeled examples are scarce?

signals.label: Settings with stronger discovered programs
signals.detail: The strongest agent-discovered programs outperform the best human-designed SSL baselines in eight of twelve evaluated settings. These are oracle-selected results.

signals.label: Largest reported improvement
signals.detail: The largest improvement reported over a strong human SSL baseline occurs in an individual dataset and label setting. It is not an average gain across tasks.

signals.label: Selection can erase gains
signals.detail: The authors report up to a 47% performance drop when their agent feedback metric is used to select a program, rather than an oracle choosing the strongest.

signals.label: Evaluated program instances
signals.detail: ProgramSelectBench collects agent-generated and human-designed SSL programs across six classification datasets, enabling further selection research.

insight.label: OPEN RESEARCH PROBLEM
insight.title: Discovering a strong program is not the same as selecting one.
insight.detail: The paper separates search quality from choosing a deployable program without trustworthy labeled validation. It also describes challenges transferring agent-discovered SSL strategies into real ecology detection tasks.

mechanisms.label: 01 / DISCOVER
mechanisms.title: Search for a learning procedure
mechanisms.explanation: An agent explores different executable SSL programs with very little labeled supervision. Search quality asks whether a strong program was found, not whether it can later be identified.

stages.label: Start with L and U
stages.detail: A small labeled set L and a larger unlabeled set U define the learning task.

stages.label: Generate programs
stages.detail: Draft, Debug, Improve and Analyze operators expand and revise executable SSL procedures.

stages.label: Guide search with feedback
stages.detail: Unsupervised signals or noisy validation help choose which candidate programs to explore.

mechanisms.takeaway: In the paper's evaluation, an oracle identifies the best discovered program using test performance. That oracle is not available for real deployment.

mechanisms.label: 02 / SELECT
mechanisms.title: Choose one program to use
mechanisms.explanation: A strong discovered candidate is only useful if the system can identify it with very few trustworthy validation labels. Selection quality is a separate problem from discovery.

stages.label: Consider the program pool
stages.detail: Discovery yields multiple candidate SSL programs, each producing a potentially different predictor.

stages.label: Estimate without oracle labels
stages.detail: Compare candidates using unsupervised metrics or actively request a limited number of labels.

stages.label: Measure selection regret
stages.detail: Compare the chosen program with the best candidate in the pool to quantify the lost test performance.

mechanisms.takeaway: The paper finds that choosing a program from weak feedback can lose much of the improvement obtained during discovery.
